A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MVI-Bench. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 18 LVLMs, caption-assisted inference and thinking comparisons, and attention-guided masking case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and additionally reports human performance and an annotation agreement analysis.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction framework, taxonomy, caption-assisted inference, and attention-guided masking procedure remain unchanged. Expanded annotation documentation does not establish a change to the underlying method.

E1.justification: Appendix D.3 extends evaluation to a human participant population comprising two high-school and two university students. The benchmark itself retains the same 624 image pairs, six VQA categories, and image-source coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds a human comparator alongside the same 18 LVLMs. Comparator membership in the caption and thinking experiments remains unchanged. HallusionBench's removal from Table 1 concerns research positioning, not an evaluated performance baseline.

E3.justification: New protocols include four participants answering all 1,248 instances in randomized order, a five-second limit, timeout-as-error scoring, and ten practice questions. Annotation agreement is assessed on 200 randomly sampled instances. Existing model decoding and answer-option shuffling settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2 adds an analysis testing annotation reliability through inter-annotator agreement and reported disagreements. Existing caption, scaling, thinking, and masking analyses remain unchanged; the supplementary example cases are retained under new figure numbers.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports Fleiss' kappa for annotation agreement and specifies averaging human accuracy across four participants. Neither version reports model-run uncertainty intervals or significance tests; no increase in model runs is established.

E6.justification: All retained model scores in Tables 2–4 are identical. Added results include human category scores, overall misleading-image accuracy of 98.24% and sensitivity of 1.63%, plus annotation kappa of 0.93 and approximately 5% reviewer disagreement.

T1.justification: Equation (1), defining MVI-Sensitivity, and the appendix's relative-attention normalization are unchanged. No new mathematical assumptions, proofs, or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces the headline finding that visual perception is the primary bottleneck with a claim that perception and reasoning are complementary. The benchmark, metric, vulnerability, and spurious-correlation contributions remain intact.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 softens perception's primacy and adds an explanation for treating captions as primarily perceptual information. New appendix passages interpret the human results as evidence of solvability without specialized knowledge and the agreement results as annotation reliability. Appendix A's limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 newly documents annotator guidelines, verification criteria, first-author review, and disagreement resolution. Appendix D.3 supplies human-study procedures. Existing caption prompts, attention implementation, model-source information, and benchmark access remain available.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning captioning, agreement measurement, in-context learning, and reasoning. It removes HallusionBench from Table 1 and the bibliography, and removes the visual-layer-selection reference. Section 2 more explicitly attributes distinctive insights to comprehensive coverage and paired evaluation.

P1.justification: v2 condenses introduction and results passages, revises author information and appendix headings, corrects the attention-implementation cross-reference, and adds acknowledgements and an impact statement. The main section sequence and much of the exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: The document adopts a substantially different conference layout, including a redesigned title block, running headers, single-column appendix text, and resized or relocated figures. It adds the vehicle-perception illustration, removes a Table 1 row, and adds a human-performance block to Table 2. Existing analytical figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: The human baseline and quantified annotation agreement add useful validation absent from v1, while fuller procedures and a more cautious perception/reasoning interpretation improve assessability. These gains are limited: the human study has only four participants, removing HallusionBench weakens prior-work completeness, and the new human resemblance sensitivity is printed as 1.99%, although Equation (1) and the reported accuracies imply 1.90%.
